mechanisms.name: shell-executor-service-seam
mechanisms.what: `ShellExecutor` is an abstract Cordis `Service` registered under the name `shell` (`ctx.shell`), declared via module augmentation of `Context` (index.ts:39-43). It defines three abstract members: `resolve(request): ShellExecSpec` (index.ts:84), `run(spec): Promise<ShellRunResult>` (index.ts:92) and `start(spec): ShellProcess` (index.ts:99), plus a `sandboxMode` getter that defaults to `undefined` (index.ts:74-76). The settings namespace constant `SHELL_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE = 'shell'` is owned here (index.ts:21) so bash and pwsh providers share one namespace without double registration.
invariants: `run` rejects only for infrastructure failures. Nonzero exits, timeout kills, and abort kills resolve with a `ShellRunResult`. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:52-53)

`start` returns immediately; no timeout applies to background processes. `done` settles at process close and never rejects; spawn failures settle as `killed` with the error on stderr. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:54-56)
`ShellProcess.readOutput` is incremental: consecutive reads never repeat output. Lossy reads report truncation and available spill files. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:57-58)

mechanisms.name: shell-cause-classification-timeout-vs-abort
mechanisms.what: `runArgv` opens ONE fused deadline with `using d = deadline(spec.signal, spec.timeoutMs, 'BASH_TIMEOUT')` and passes `d.signal` into the spawn. After the handle settles it computes `timedOut = timeoutOf(d.signal, 'BASH_TIMEOUT') !== undefined` and `aborted = d.signal.aborted && !timedOut`, and returns those booleans plus the effective `timeoutMs` on the result. mechanisms.name: terminal-send-interrupt-on-cancel

mechanisms.name: e2b-base64-output-transport
mechanisms.what: Remote stdout/stderr travel as newline-delimited base64 frames produced by `OUTPUT_ENCODER_SOURCE`, a Node one-liner piped to `node -e` inside the wrapper (with `head -c <maxSpillBytes>` and `tee` writing the private spill file first when the mode has a spill). `E2BBase64Decoder.push(text)` buffers arbitrarily split SDK callbacks, splits on `\n`, rejects a frame that is not valid base64 or that does not round-trip (`bytes.toString('base64') !== frame`), recognizes the reserved `E2B_OUTPUT_COMPLETE_FRAME` as clean EOF, and throws on a duplicate completion or on any frame after completion. `finish(requireComplete)` throws `truncated base64 output transport` when a partial frame remains and `incomplete output transport` when the EOF frame never arrived; a requested termination passes `requireComplete = false` to discard the interrupted tail.

mechanisms.what: Termination and quiescence are proved with control-plane probes keyed on a numeric PGID. `groupAlive` runs `ps -eo pgid=,stat= | awk '$1 == <pid> && $2 !~ /^[ZXx]/ { live=1 } END { if (live) print "live" }'` and treats `SandboxNotFoundError` as 'not alive'. `terminate()` aborts the internal `terminationController`, destroys the host pipes and starts `terminateRemote()` once; `terminateGroup` sends `TERM` to the group, waits for group exit within `spec.graceMs`, and on failure escalates to `SIGKILL` via `forceKillGroup` (group `kill -KILL` **and** `handle.kill()`), then requires `waitForGroupExit` to prove emptiness or throws `remote process group <id> remained live after force termination`. `waitForExit(signal)` blocks until the group is gone. `signalRemoteGroups` is the single tolerant signal path: it swallows `CommandExitError` (groups already gone) and `SandboxNotFoundError`.

Notable cross-package facts: (1) `DSH_ENV_PREFIX` is re-exported from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess` by packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:13 and used to build the reserved keys at packages/shell/shell-env/src/index.ts:70-72 — its literal value is defined in the subprocess package, not here. (3) tool-bash-persistent and tool-pwsh-persistent do NOT use `ctx.shell`; they depend only on `ctx.terminals`, so persistent sessions bypass executor config (timeoutMs/maxOutputBytes/graceMs/sandboxMode) entirely. ### _shell_partB.json — subprocess/* (packages/subprocess/subprocess, packages/subprocess/subprocess-local)
All 15 .ts files of packages/subprocess/subprocess and packages/subprocess/subprocess-local were read in full. Observations worth carrying forward: (1) `spawnSubprocess` in spawn.ts uses the detached-PGID/taskkill fallback owner; the Windows Job Object path is reached only through `LocalSubprocessRuntime.spawn` -> `selectContainmentMode` -> `launchWindowsJob`, i.e. the Job runner is a parent+child process pair, not an in-process binding. (2) `windows-inspector.ts` also uses koffi/kernel32 directly (Toolhelp32 + GetProcessTimes + WaitForSingleObject) and does NOT use a Job Object — Job handling lives in packages/subprocess/win32-process (`spawnCurrentTokenJobProcess`, `terminateJob`, `isJobEmpty`, `probeCurrentTokenJobSupport`), which is audited separately. (3) `OutputCollector.finalize()` is exported/used by the seam path but `readFrom` is what the shell executors actually call (via `SubprocessOutputReader`). (4) The Linux `started` identity field index 19 is 0-based into the post-comm remainder, i.e. field 22 of the stat line. (5) `runner-launch.ts` reaches outside its package for `../../../../tsconfig.base.json` when running from source (line 20).

### _shell_partC.json — packages/subprocess/win32-process
All 5 .ts files read in full. Facts to carry into the inventory: (1) Job termination is implemented three ways here — `terminateJob`/`TerminateJobObject` (process.ts:596-598), kill-on-close via the Job limit (process.ts:333-352), and per-process `TerminateProcess` on failure paths. (2) The Job is unnamed and created per spawn (`CreateJobObjectW(null, null)`). (3) `spawnPipedProcess` (restricted-token, piped stdout/stderr) is exported but the ordinary Windows path used by subprocess-local is `spawnCurrentTokenJobProcess`; the piped variant's production caller (if any) is outside this package. ### _shell_partD.json — packages/terminal/terminal, packages/terminal/terminal-bash, packages/terminal/tool-terminal
All 8 .ts files read in full. Cross-package facts worth carrying: (1) `terminal-bash` depends directly on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-local` for `resolvePwshPath` and `ENCODING_PREAMBLE` (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:4 and src/index.ts:16) — a packages/terminal -> packages/shell dependency. (2) `terminal-bash` reaches the PTY through `ctx.subprocess.spawnTerminal`, so all the subprocess-local containment/identity machinery applies underneath. (3) `isStdinWaiting` from the subprocess inspector is the exact-probe evidence the readiness machine consumes via `SubprocessTerminalForeground.inputWaiting` (session.ts:500); on macOS and Windows that probe always returns false (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts:506 and windows-inspector.ts:96), so only the prompt-marker and idle-silence paths can settle there. (4) `tool-bash-persistent`/`tool-pwsh-persistent` consume this service only through `ctx.terminals.spawn/startSend/read/kill/list`. (5) The `idleSilenceMs` default (3_000) is the only 'idle timeout' in this group; the absolute per-send bound is `timeoutMs` (30_000).

### _shell_partE.json — packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b
All 6 .ts files read in full. Facts to carry: (1) This package is the remote twin of `subprocess-local` and shares only the seam types and `SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN`; there is no Win32/Job, no /proc inspection, and no identity fencing — quiescence is proven by re-running `ps` in the sandbox (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:651-661, terminal.ts:146-174). (2) Process-group identity is a numeric PGID read from a file that a same-UID sandbox process could rewrite; the code guards only against ids <= 1 and documents the residual reuse race in a TODO (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:493-498, remote.ts:87-88). (3) `E2BSubprocessHandle.spawn` is synchronous by contract while the remote command starts asynchronously, hence the `commandState`/`readyState` resolver pair and `DeferredStdin` (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/process.ts:51-69, :166-167). (4) Unlike subprocess-local, this provider has no 'fallback' containment tier: every ordinary spawn and terminal is always group/session-contained. (5) The `exit 125` sentinel appears twice (bootstrap tool check and the terminal runner's empty-argv check) and is not translated into a Node error code.
